title: sarcolobus subnudus
intro: Sarcolobus subnudus, commonly known as Indian snakeroot, is a plant species belonging to the Apocynaceae family, native to India and Southeast Asia. It has been traditionally used in Ayurvedic medicine to treat various health conditions, including fever, rheumatism, and skin disorders, due to its numerous health benefits, such as anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial properties. The therapeutic actions of Sarcolobus subnudus include reducing fever, alleviating pain, and promoting wound healing, which are attributed to its bioactive constituents, including alkaloids, glycosides, and saponins. Research has identified the presence of bioactive compounds like sarcolin, snakeroot alkaloids, and glycosides, which contribute to the plant's medicinal properties.
